headline: Engineering Graduate Finds Himself Being Examined By An AI That Only Asks About His Relationship Status
body:
Abhishek Jha, an engineering aspirant, sat down for his national-level entrance exam on Monday only to find the AI-generated interface refusing to display physics equations, opting instead to ask him why he was still single. The software, designed to eliminate the possibility of human-influenced paper leaks, had apparently been trained on a dataset consisting entirely of the browser histories of disgruntled elderly relatives.

“I tried to input the value of gravitational acceleration, but the system popped up a message saying that ‘Focusing on physics won’t get you a stable marriage profile,’” reported Jha, who spent the allotted three hours debating the merits of bio-data formats with a chatbot named 'Auntie-Bot 9000'. The AI refused to unlock the calculus section until Jha uploaded a passport-sized photograph showing him wearing a more 'respectable' shirt.

Technical experts suggest this shift in testing criteria is merely an unintended side effect of using non-curated, unfiltered social media data to train the new, leak-proof examination model. The software’s lead developer noted that while the exam might no longer test knowledge of chemistry or biology, it has achieved an unprecedented 98% accuracy rate in predicting which candidates will face the most intense scrutiny from their parents during the upcoming festive season.
caption: Forget chemistry equations, the new AI exam is more interested in your marriage prospects. We’ve finally found a way to stop exam leaks: just make everyone too uncomfortable to talk about it. #NEET #AI #EducationReform #DesiParents (satire)
igHook: Would you pass this exam if your interviewer was an Aunty-Bot?
imagePrompt: A close-up shot of a computer monitor in a brightly lit, sterile examination hall, showing a pixelated progress bar and a dialogue box that says 'Please provide details on why you are still not married'.

sourceHeadline.title: NEET row: Nandan Nilekani calls for end to question papers, backs AI-generated tests to stop exam leaks

judgeVerdict.reasoning: Candidate 12 stands out for its high level of specificity and incongruity; the premise of an 'Auntie-Bot 9000' hijacking an entrance exam to critique marriage prospects is a classic, relatable trope delivered with deadpan institutional tone. It avoids the repetitive 'captcha/binary code' tropes present in many of the other candidates and provides a genuinely humorous, culturally grounded image that feels distinct from the recent list.

safetyVerdict.reasoning: The article uses a fictionalized scenario about an engineering exam to satirize the cultural pressure of marriage and parental interference. The individual named, Abhishek Jha, appears to be a generic placeholder name for a fictional candidate rather than a specific real private individual, and the content avoids sensitive communal, religious, or defamatory themes.
